verdict.rationale: Stripe Issuing documents its own spending controls, which set spending limits per authorization or per month and block merchant categories, countries, merchant IDs and card presence. This is the platform-enforced amount-cap core of the story, but the evidence does not show the other scopes, windows or count rules the story asks for. Missing for 10: per-cardholder (vs per-card) limit scope, daily and all-time windows, transaction-count velocity rules, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can set spend limits per card and per cardholder — amount caps over daily, monthly, or all-time windows, and transaction-count velocity rules — enforced by the platform, not my code

citations.quote: You can use spending controls to block merchant categories (for example, bakeries), countries, merchant IDs, or card presence, and to set spending limits per authorization or per month.
with spend controls, real-time authorization decisioning, and full transaction visibility
